thread:
Maya: FYI noticed p95 decode time jumped ~1.7x after yesterday's runtime merge (commit f3a9b2c).
Samir: ugh. is this the kernel-selector tweak or the fused-ops landing?
Maya: suspect kernel-selector. The change added a new heuristic for preferring 'wide-attn-v2' on short sequences. Repro with small prompt workload shows consistent slowdown.
Yuan: any CI numbers? I saw an alert but no trace yet.
CI Bot: Perf CI job perf/decode/20260317-11 failed: p95 decode +72% vs baseline. Link: https://ci.internal/perf/20260317-11
Priya: can you paste the failing job config / model + batch sizes?
Maya: baseline: model=redwood/llama-2-7b, seq=64, batch=4, tokens/sec dropped from 12.3k -> 7.1k, p95 went 22ms -> 38ms. Repro script: `./bench/decode_bench --model r/llama-2-7b --seq 64 --batch 4 --iters 200` — run on an A100.
Leo: thanks. can you dump which kernel was chosen during the run? we added logging but it's noisy.
Maya: attached minimal log snippet (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-17T15:02:31Z] kernel_selector: chose wide-attn-v2 for seq=64 batch=4
[2026-03-17T15:02:31Z] runtime: fused-ops enabled=true
[2026-03-17T15:02:31Z] decode: p95=38.2ms
```
Yuan: I ran a perf flamegraph with `perf` and nvprof. The hot path is in the attention kernel (reduce + reorder) when wide-attn-v2 is used; the previous wide-attn-v1 spends more time in matmul but has better memory layout for KV caching. Attaching top hot functions:
```
attn_reorder_kernel  42%
kv_cache_write       18%
matmul_fused         12%
```
Samir: so selector picked v2 which is worse for KV-heavy decode. Does the selector consider KV cache write cost? I thought we added a heuristic for memory-coalescing but maybe tradeoff wrong.
Maya: looks like the heuristic only considered tile occupancy and HBM throughput, not the incremental KV write cost per token. For short sequences the cost of repeated KV writes dominates.
Priya: options: revert the selector change, or gate it behind rollout flag and pin canary to previous heuristic.
Leo: for quick mitigation — we can set env KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE=wide-attn-v1 in the canary config. That should restore perf while we bisect.
Maya: agreed. patch prepared: `revert: kernel-selector heuristic` in branch revert/kernel-selector-shortseq. But we should bisect to be sure it's the only cause.
Samir: can we bisect between f3a9b2c and the commit that added fused-ops? timeline?
Maya: fused-ops landed earlier (b9d4f00). The selector change is f3a9b2c. Bisect range b9d4f00..f3a9b2c.
Yuan: I'll run a binary-search local bisect script to test decode perf quickly across commits. Using `./tools/bisect_perf --cmd "./bench/decode_bench ..." --metric p95 --threshold 1.3`
CI Bot: Note: automatic bisect infra scheduled run at 2026-03-17T17:00Z. Result will post here.
Priya: plan: 1) Hold canary rollout (pause) 2) Force selector=v1 in running canaries 3) Run bisect + flamegraphs 4) If bisect points to selector change, revert and roll forward with tests.
Samir: sounds good. Maya can you add a short reproducer that runs inside the CI container? makes it easier for SRE to run.
Maya: yep uploading `repro/decode_shortseq.sh` to the PR.
Leo: also add a small unit test that simulates KV cache write penalty model so selector doesn't regress again.
Maya: will add. quick note: observed smaller models (1.3b) show no regression because KV writes are cheaper vs attn kernel costs — makes sense.
Yuan: running the bisect now on local 2x A100. Will report back in ~25m. :eyes:
Samir: thanks. if bisect is noisy, we can add a micro-benchmark that pins seq/batch to isolate.
CI Bot: Bisect run started (job 20260317-bisect-1). Updates will appear in thread.
Maya: thumbs if you agree with the rollback-first mitigation so customer SLAs aren't impacted. :thumbsup:
Priya: +1
Leo: +1

Yuan: +1

Maya: confirmed. I'll open the revert PR and also a follow-up that tweaks the heuristic to include estimated KV write cost.
